title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young Andalusian shepherd named Santiago leaves Spain after recurring dreams suggest a hidden treasure awaits him near the Egyptian pyramids. Along the journey he meets mentors, merchants, and mystics who teach him about destiny, courage, and listening to his heart. The novel follows his search for treasure while revealing a deeper quest for purpose and self-discovery.

title: Pather Panchali
author: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
description: Set in rural Bengal, the story follows Apu and his family as they struggle with poverty, hope, and changing circumstances. Through Apu's curious eyes, readers witness childhood adventures, family bonds, and heartbreaking losses. The novel paints a vivid picture of village life while exploring resilience and dreams.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: Stephen Hawking introduces readers to some of the biggest questions in physics, including the origins of the universe, black holes, and the nature of time. Using accessible explanations, he connects complex scientific ideas to everyday curiosity. The book explores humanity's effort to understand how the cosmos works.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: This influential science book examines evolution through the perspective of genes rather than individual organisms. Dawkins explains how natural selection shapes behavior, cooperation, and competition across species. The work challenged conventional thinking and remains a major contribution to evolutionary biology.

title: Principles of Accounting
author: Belverd E. Needles
description: A foundational academic text that introduces accounting concepts, financial statements, bookkeeping procedures, and business reporting. Through practical examples and case studies, it helps students understand how organizations record and analyze financial information. It serves as a strong starting point for accounting education.

title: Microeconomics
author: N. Gregory Mankiw
description: This academic book explores how individuals, households, and firms make economic decisions. It explains supply and demand, market structures, pricing, and public policy using real-world examples. The text is widely used in universities for building a strong understanding of economic theory.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: Harari traces the history of Homo sapiens from prehistoric hunter-gatherers to the modern globalized world. The book examines how shared beliefs, cultures, and institutions shaped civilizations. It combines history, anthropology, and philosophy to explain humanity's remarkable rise.

title: The Guns of August
author: Barbara W. Tuchman
description: This historical work chronicles the dramatic opening month of World War I. Through detailed storytelling, Tuchman explains how military plans, political decisions, and human errors pushed Europe into a devastating conflict. The narrative reveals how quickly events spiraled beyond control.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Paul Atreides arrives on the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of a valuable substance that powers interstellar civilization. As political betrayal threatens his family, Paul becomes entangled in prophecy, survival, and rebellion. The novel blends science fiction with themes of power, ecology, and destiny.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: After being left behind on Mars following a mission disaster, astronaut Mark Watney must rely on science, engineering, and determination to stay alive. While NASA works to bring him home, he faces countless challenges in the harsh environment. The story combines suspense, humor, and scientific problem-solving.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: James Clear explains how tiny behavioral changes can produce remarkable long-term results. Through practical frameworks and real-life examples, he shows how habits are formed, maintained, and improved. The book focuses on building systems that make success more consistent and sustainable.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
description: Covey presents a framework for personal and professional effectiveness based on character, responsibility, and long-term thinking. Each habit encourages readers to improve relationships, leadership, and decision-making. The book remains a classic in personal development literature.

author: George Orwell
description: In a dystopian future ruled by a totalitarian regime, Winston Smith struggles with truth, freedom, and individuality. Constant surveillance and manipulation shape every aspect of society. As Winston begins to question authority, he faces the consequences of resisting a powerful state.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: Carl Sagan takes readers on a journey through space, time, and scientific discovery. The book explores stars, galaxies, evolution, and humanity's place in the universe. Its engaging storytelling inspires curiosity about science and the wonders of the cosmos.

title: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn
description: Rather than focusing on political leaders alone, Zinn tells American history from the perspectives of workers, minorities, and social movements. The book examines major events through the experiences of ordinary people. It offers an alternative lens on the development of the United States.
